Textbooks
Required:
•    Principles of Macroeconomics, 6th Ed., by Robert Frank, Ben Bernanke, Kate Antonovics, Ori
     Heffetz, McGraw-Hill Education; 6th edition (2015). ISBN-13: 978-0073518992

Recommended:
•    Principles of Economics, 7th Ed., by N. Gregory Mankiw, South-Western College Pub; 7th
     edition (2014), ISBN-13: 978-1285165875
•   Economics, 4th Edition, by Paul Krugman and Robin Wells, Worth Publishers. 5th Edition
     (2017). ISBN-13: 978-1464143847


Course Description
Macroeconomics is the study of the economy as a whole, to understand how it behaves and what
affects  it. Macroeconomics analyses and explains issues  like economic growth,  interest  rates,
unemployment, inflation, and business cycles. The study of Macroeconomics allows the government
to decide what its economic policy should be, and allows business environment. Macroeconomic
questions include: What affects the long term growth rate of GDP? What can the government do to
affect the unemployment rate? What causes inflation? These and other questions will be addressed in
this course.
By the end of the course, students should be able to:
•   Define the various basic macroeconomic terms and concepts and synthesize them into a coherent
    macroeconomic structure.
•   Analyze and predict the behavior of the aggregate economy in the short run and in the long run;
     including how various policies and events affect the markets for labor, loanable funds, and

general goods and services, and how this influences the key macroeconomic variables: inflation,
    unemployment, and GDP.
•   Be aware of the recent history and current macroeconomic environment of major countries
    around the world, especially that of China, Europe, and the US; and be able to discuss current
    macroeconomic affairs by applying the concepts and theories from this course.


Quizzes
Weekly quizzes of multiple choices questions are hosted on Blackboard (BB) starting from the first
week and will be opened at 12:30am every Monday, with a deadline of submission at 11:59pm on
Sunday of the same week. You can submit your quiz answers unlimited times, and the highest grade
will be counted. The online grading system is programmed to stop accepting quiz submissions as soon
as the deadline arrives, so make sure to complete them on time. No late submission will be accepted
for any reason.


Assignments
Weekly problem sets with free response questions will be posted on BB at 12:30am every Monday,
starting from the second week, and are to be handed in with a deadline of submission at 11:59pm on
Sunday  of  the same week.  All  assignment answers  should be uploaded  to BB under  the
corresponding submission link. Here are some general policy for the submission:
1. Please upload one PDF file with your full name or student ID displayed in the file name.
2. All answers must be in English. Answers in other languages will not be graded.
3. Please mark question numbers clearly in the answers and make sure that the content of the PDF file
is clear and readable. Unidentified or unreadable answers will not be graded.
4. Copying is not allowed. Please refer to the detailed policies on Academic Integrity.
5. No late submission will be accepted for any reason. It is the students’ responsibility to ensure
that the assignments are submitted successfully before the deadline.
  To prevent internet problems that may cause late submission, here are some advices and policies:
    •  Do not wait until the last minute to turn in the assignment. Leave at least a 30-60 minutes
      window to double-check that the files are uploaded successfully. Please do not close your
       browser until the file is fully uploaded.
    •   Students are allowed to upload answer files unlimited times and overwrite the old files.
        Therefore, one safe way to prevent late submission is to upload an initial version early and
      make necessary changes until the deadline. No updates will be accepted after the deadline.
    •   In the special case that BB system breaks down, student can directly send an email to the
        course TA with the answer file attached before the deadline. Email received after the deadline
        will not be accepted.

Examination
There will be a midterm exam and a final exam, both onsite and close-book. Students who are unable
to take midterm or final exams for medical or other compelling reasons should seek endorsements
from instructors with the evidence documentation, and then upload the approval from the instructor
and the evidence documentation in Student Information System (SIS) within 5 working days after
the original exam. Note that absence from exam due to misremembering the exam time or getting up
late would not be approved. The final approval for absence from midterm exams lies with course
instructors, and the approval for absence from centralized final exam lies with the Registry. Failing to
properly follow the absence application procedure will cause a grade of zero towards the exam.

There will NOT be any make-ups given for the midterm exam. With an approval of absence from the
midterm exam (following the above policy and procedure), the weight of midterm exam will be
placed onto the final exam. Make-up exam for the final exam will be completed within 15 calendar
days after centralized exam week. Students need to receive an official approval from the Registry
(via SIS) of the absence from the final exam in order to join the make-up exam. Only under
extraordinary circumstance a make-up exam taken after 15 days may be allowed by the instructor.
However, the late make-up final will be worth 50% ~ 80% of the points earned depending on the
circumstances.


Grading Policy
               Component              % weight
                  Quizzes                       10%
                 Assignments                    10%
                Midterm Exam                   30%
                    Final Exam                     50%


Academic Integrity
Students are encouraged to form study groups and are allowed to discuss assignments. Copying is
NOT allowed. Academic dishonesty includes, but is not limited to, cheating, plagiarizing, failure to
cite referenced sources, fabricating information or citations, facilitating acts of academic dishonesty
by others, having unauthorized possession of examinations, submitting work of another person or
work previously used without informing the instructor, or tampering with academic work of
other students. Any breach of academic integrity will be reported and there will be a penalty in the
course grade.
